To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the scaling exponents of DGC and its components are similar in insects of different size, (ii) the temperature dependence of DGC frequency is the primary mechanism for temperature‐associated increases of V̇co, and (iii) the relationship between ventilation phases and total DGC duration are better described using proportions rather than phase coefficients.

the scaling exponents of V̇co 2 and O‐phase emission volumes are not affected by temperature, and that the temperature‐dependent modulation of V̇CO 2 is achieved by increases in DCG frequency rather than increases in O‐phase volumes.

DGC frequency, F‐phase, O‐phase, and DGC durations are all closely coupled to DCG duration, and that the proportionality of each phase of a DGC to the DGC duration can be used as an estimate of the contribution of each phase to the total DGC duration.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, while the DGC is a highly conserved trait among insects, the scaling of the DGC and the way in which the DGC is modulated by temperature vary among species.
, although DGC are a common feature of insect gas exchange, their characteristics and the way in which they are affected by temperature vary considerably across insect species.
, while DGC frequency and V̇co₂ are strongly influenced by temperature, the O‐phase volumes of DGC are not.
